# Results — Study 818 (Trend Factor)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Han, Zhou
& Zhu (2016): a **trend factor** that blends normalized moving-average signals across seven
horizons (3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 days), weighted by rolling cross-sectional (Fama-MacBeth)
slopes, forecasts the cross-section of returns better than any single moving-average timing
rule or momentum, so a long-high-trend / short-low-trend book earns a positive spread. Offline
& deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `5384b8f7f128` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's seven normalized moving averages **`A_L = MA_L(price) / price`** for `L ∈ {3,5,10,20,50,100,200}`; each day a cross-sectional OLS of the realized next return on the `A_L` vector gives predictive slopes, and the **250-day rolling average of past slopes** is dotted into today's `A_L` vector → the fitted expected return (the **trend factor**), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the trend factor; **long the top 30%** (high trend), **short the bottom 30%** (low trend), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled high-vs-low books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a two-era cut; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. The trend
factor is documented largely on the broad CRSP cross-section (thousands of small names); a
50-mega-cap survivor panel is a thin, efficient slice where a blended MA signal has the least
room to add value — which is what we find.

## The headline — long-high-trend / short-low-trend spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% trend-factor spread (n = **3,697** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long high-trend − short low-trend)** | **+1.42 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+0.99** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.87 |
| high-trend book / low-trend book | +8.48 bps / +7.06 bps (Welch *t* = +0.49) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.23 |

The claimed edge **does not replicate.** The spread has the *right sign* — high-trend names
did edge out low-trend names — but it is **statistically indistinguishable from zero**
(NW *t* = +0.99, well under the desk's |t| ≥ 2 bar), and its gross Sharpe of +0.23 is a rounding
error. On 50 liquid mega-caps the seven-horizon blend simply has no reliable predictive content.

## Contrast — the two things the trend factor is *claimed to beat*

The paper's headline is that the blended trend factor **dominates** single-MA timing and
momentum. On this universe the ranking is the reverse:

| sort | spread/day | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **trend factor (blend of 7 MAs)** | **+1.42 bps** | **+0.99** |
| single-MA(200) timing | +2.01 bps | +1.24 |
| 12-1 cross-sectional momentum | +2.24 bps | +1.40 |

All three are insignificant, but the **blended trend factor is the *weakest* of the three** —
the exact opposite of the paper's central claim. The extra machinery (seven horizons, rolling
Fama-MacBeth slopes) buys nothing over a plain 200-day timing rule or vanilla momentum here.

## Placebo — is the (tiny, right-sign) spread even a real alignment of the sort?

Keep the trend-factor sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+1.42 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.019 bps (0.964) |
| position of observed | ≈ **+1.45 sd from the mean** (right-tail p = **0.066**) |

The observed spread sits only ~1.45 sd into the right tail of the permutation null (p = 0.066) —
so even *before* costs, the sort's edge is not cleanly separable from a lucky alignment.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,563) | +1.72 bps | +0.96 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +1.20 bps | +0.57 |

Weak in both halves and *fading* in the recent era — no sign of a durable premium.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +1.42 bps | 2.14 bps | **−0.72 bps** | −0.44 | −0.11 | −1.8%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +1.42 bps | 10.14 bps | **−8.72 bps** | −5.34 | −1.39 | −22.0%/yr |

The +1.42 bps/day gross edge is *already smaller than* the 2.14 bps/day round-trip friction at a
mere 1 bp one-way: the book is **net negative** even under featherweight costs, and bleeds
−22%/yr at a realistic 5 bps. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "trend state" that (with `edge>0`) is added
to the daily return, so the price genuinely trends AND the trend predicts the next return. No
network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.07** (sd 0.94), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0015`, seed 818) | **+10.28** (Welch *t* = +10.64) |

The fitted trend factor recovers a *planted* Han-Zhou-Zhu relation cleanly (*t* = +10.28) and
stays silent on the null (fires at the nominal ~5% rate) — so the flat real-tape result is a
genuine absence of signal, not a broken detector. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The celebrated trend factor does **not** replicate on 50 liquid US
  mega-caps. The specified long-high-trend / short-low-trend spread is **+1.42 bps/day**
  (NW *t* = **+0.99**) — the right sign but statistically indistinguishable from zero, only
  ~1.45 sd into a 1,000-permutation placebo (p = 0.066), weak-and-fading across both eras
  (*t* = +0.96 / +0.57). Worse for the claim, the blended factor is the **weakest** of the three
  sorts it is said to beat (single-MA(200) *t* = +1.24, momentum *t* = +1.40). A clean 20-seed
  synthetic control confirms the machinery is unbiased, so this is a true null on the mega-cap
  survivor slice, not a bug. The trend premium is a broad-cross-section / small-cap phenomenon.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The +1.42 bps/day gross edge is smaller than the 2.14 bps/day
  round-trip friction at 1 bp one-way, so the book is net negative (−0.72 bps/day) even under
  featherweight costs and loses −22%/yr at 5 bps. Nothing to trade.
